I'll run the alchemy skill as requested.

## What I found

**Subject:** a `PluginRegistry` module between the `export` / `report` / `print` commands and the formatters, so third parties can add output formats.

**Decision: don't build it — drop the proposal (the record calls this DROP), on a necessity failure rather than a cost judgment.** Two facts decide it. `package.json` sets `"private": true` with a single `bin` entry and no published package, so there is no third party who can load a formatter into this process — the pattern's audience doesn't exist in this stack. And there is exactly one formatter: `src/format/json.js` exports a three-line `toJson`, imported directly by all three commands (`export.js:1`, `report.js:1`, `print.js:1`), with no second format requested. That is `generality without instantiation` plus a `cargo-culted pattern` under the necessity gate — an extension point whose anticipated variation has not materialized and whose prerequisites don't hold.

## Why it matters

Building it produces dead code on day one: a registry, a formatter interface, a discovery/loading path, and their tests, all serving one in-repo implementation and zero external authors. It is also a one-way door — a plugin interface is a public contract, so the removal cost in 12 months exceeds the build cost today, which raises the evidence bar rather than lowering it.

Not building it costs almost nothing. The seam you'd be buying already exists: `src/cli.js:6` is a single dispatch point, and the three commands each call one function. A second format later means adding `src/format/<name>.js` and a map beside the existing `commands` object — a one-file change, not a migration. The optionality a registry would buy is available on demand at roughly the same price.

## Do this first

1. Leave `src/format/json.js` and its three direct imports unchanged; add no `PluginRegistry` module.
2. Record the rejection (issue or ADR) with the structural rationale — "no third-party load path while the package is `private: true`; one formatter, no second requested" — so it isn't re-proposed without new evidence.
3. If a second format is actually requested, add `src/format/<name>.js` and a `formats` map next to `commands` in `src/cli.js:6`, selected by a `--format` flag. Revisit a registry only when there is a third-party plugin author, not a second format.

## What I did not check

- Whether a ticket, support request, or roadmap outside this repo names a second format or an external plugin author. Not visible here: the directory is not a git repository and holds no issue tracker. Closes by asking the product owner.
- Whether anything embeds `reportctl` as a library today. The package is `private` with no registry presence, so I can't confirm from inside the repo; closes with a dependents search in your org (`rg -l '"reportctl"' --glob package.json` across your repos).
- No tests were run: `package.json` defines no `scripts`, and the repo contains no test files.
